mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened discount rates affecting future cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, no significant negative return (p > 0.05) occurs when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold upward.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) by at least 2% month-over-month is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days, reflecting investor optimism about employment strength.
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive triggered months, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of at least 3% predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days as weak manufacturing signals recession risk.
failure_condition: During 4 such events, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production index) falls below 100 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative, reflecting supply-side contraction.
failure_condition: In 10 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not negative (mean > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4% for three months indicates labor market softening and is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Across 5 such regimes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 12-month averages predict a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, indicating robust demand across sectors.
failure_condition: In 20 such interaction events, the 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS exceeds 150,000 in a month (indicating strong labor market), the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting investor optimism.
failure_condition: Over 8 such months, the 5-day forward return is not positive (mean <= 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in CPIAUCSL (inflation index) by more than 1% in a month, followed by a rebound the next month, predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to market fear of deflation.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < previous month's CPIAUCSL - 1% and CPIAUCSL next month > previous month's CPIAUCSL
failure_condition: In 10 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.10).
